topic: Fix p>=2 and equally spaced times 0,h,2h,3h. Let X(t)=exp(tG)(X(0)-x*)+x* with real Hurwitz G in the principal-log alias strip, Gaussian X(0), and independent unpaired observations Y_k=X(kh)+epsilon_k with one unknown common E>0 and no process noise. Restrict to strict positive adjacent covariance decreases. Prove the complete covariance-difference orthogonal-stabilizer classification of compatible V=exp(hG), including block Gram feasibility, O(m-r) fibers, stability/logarithm/Stein/E-positivity filters, finite sign enumeration, and global uniqueness certification. Prove three snapshots have generic continuous ambiguity for p>=3 while four identify generically by a rational Krylov map; classify exceptional fibers, show exponentially many admissible explanations can occur, identify information nullity with stabilizer dimension, and derive perturbation bounds plus branchwise moment inference on regular strata. Use covar_lin_dyn as the supplied-noise consumer. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The stabilizer/admissibility proofs and Krylov recovery were derived; exact checks passed 105 legal models/relabelings, four p=3 rotations preserving three snapshots, a four-snapshot continuous fiber, a two-model finite fiber, the supplied rational witness, and 60 perturbations. No matching common-noise theorem was found in Aalto, Wang, QWENDY v4, Morimoto-Kashima, or Inoue. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Construct a certified initializer and labeling rule for noncyclic finite branches with quantitative separation from excluded branches; current local residual estimators are implicit. EARLY KILL TEST: Recover the p=2 witness by K1 K0 inverse; reproduce the exact p=3 t=1/100 rotation with positive E and changed fourth covariance; verify exactly two legal p=2 completions; ensure empirical estimation never requires exact sample spectrum or probe-Gram equality. open_problems.why_unsolved: Aalto–Lamoline–Gonçalves leave an orthogonal matrix, or repeated-eigenvalue orthogonal blocks, after whitening their covariance equations, but assume known propagated noise and allow observation covariance to be subtracted only when known. In the common-E unpaired regime, differencing removes E from congruences but E returns through level-covariance positivity and Stein reconstruction, so orthogonal completion, stability, the logarithm cut, and E-positivity must be classified jointly. The prior Hawkes and BACKSHIFT constructions confirm that lag quotients and covariance differencing can recover mechanisms, but their one-sided restricted-log and joint-diagonalizer arguments do not solve this two-sided temporal congruence fiber. The scan found no paper proving the resulting common-E classification; this nonoccupation is an inference from the bounded scan.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Exact population ranks, probe-Gram identities, and spectral matches fail almost surely for empirical moments, while the legal population set can contain several isolated branches selected by stability, logarithm, Stein, and positivity inequalities. Aalto et al. give local sensitivity at one optimum and Morimoto–Kashima give an iterative fit, but neither certifies all global branches. The prior catalogue separately leaves output-sensitive quotient enumeration, residual-tolerant outer families, and basis-invariant rank-truncation inference open. Adapting alpha-certification first requires eliminating stabilizer variables into a zero-dimensional system, proving completeness of real roots, and adding interval-certified inequality and matrix-log filters; a branch label is stable only with a computable gap to every excluded branch.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An output-sensitive algorithm which, under explicit Jacobian and branch-separation margins, returns certified disjoint neighborhoods containing all and only admissible finite branches, labels them continuously under perturbation, and yields simultaneous branchwise root-n confidence regions with stated coverage.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Regular-stratum delta methods do not cover triangular arrays on which a simple Gram block becomes repeated, an isolated branch merges with another, or an O(m-r) stabilizer appears. The covariance-shift proposal records that bounded scalar information distance does not determine local certification power because distinct collision paths can have different tangent cones, and the Hawkes proposal leaves honest adaptation over its rank boundary open. open_problems.why_unsolved: Unknown Q enters every covariance recursion and changes the whitening eigenspaces used to recover V, while common E is added only at observation. Kong et al. show that even with temporal correlations and known dynamics, joint noise-covariance identification requires rank and decoupling conditions; Odelson et al. exploit time-series autocovariances unavailable under destructive unpaired sampling. Hence adjacent marginal-covariance differences no longer eliminate both nuisance components, and neither literature determines whether additional transient marginals restore injectivity. Nonoccupation of the joint unknown-(V,Q,E) snapshot regime is an inference from the bounded scan.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Necessary-and-sufficient rank or Gram conditions and a minimal-snapshot theorem for the map (V,Q,E,Sigma0) to the marginal covariance sequence, yielding either a constructive identifying formula and fiber classification or an explicit nonidentification family in every insufficient regime.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Exact cancellation of common additive covariance is the first load-bearing step of the snapshot construction. If E varies with time, adjacent differences mix latent dynamical change with unknown nuisance drift, so the Gram and stabilizer equations no longer hold and point identification can fail even away from the original exceptional strata. The cited failed proposal names this exact measurement-error failure and its reviewer asks for residual-tolerant outer families, but its covariance-shift model does not derive the dynamic recursion or sharp set for a stable transition. Bounded or low-rank drift therefore creates a concrete partial-identification problem, not merely a numerical perturbation of the point-identified formula.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp set-valued characterization, or matching computable inner and outer bounds, for all stable principal-strip transitions compatible with the snapshots and the stated E-drift class, with collapse to the common-E fiber as the drift radius tends to zero.

The first proof step that changes is replacing reconstruction from several discrete input-output models by simultaneous unequal-lag covariance-congruence equations sharing E and G. literature_map:
Aalto–Lamoline–Gonçalves (2022, Systems & Control Letters) is the closest exact-ID anchor: covariance congruences yield orthogonal/block-orthogonal fibers, but propagated noise is known and observation noise is handled only when known.
Aalto–Gonçalves (2019, arXiv:1903.06540) established the ensemble-snapshot system-identification setting motivated by destructive single-cell measurements.
Wang–Al-Radhawi–Lauffenburger–Sontag (2024, npj Systems Biology and Applications) prove a three-time-point frontier for deterministic affine snapshot dynamics and treat measurement noise computationally rather than as an unknown common covariance fiber.
Morimoto–Kashima (2025, L4DC) supply an EM-like Schrödinger-bridge estimator for linear Gaussian snapshot marginals, but not a complete uniqueness theorem.
Inoue–Inoue–Kashima–Onogi (2026, NOLTA) use few snapshots for covariance steering and numerical model recovery rather than common-measurement-noise identification.
QWENDY v4 (arXiv:2503.09605) uses four supplied covariance matrices and extra covariance information to resolve signs, but does not identify an unknown common additive E.
Odelson–Rajamani–Rawlings (2006, Automatica) estimate Q and R by constrained autocovariance least squares with dynamics supplied.
Kong et al. (2022, Systems & Control Letters, arXiv:2202.04963) prove nonuniqueness of Q/R under one autocovariance-least-squares formulation.
Kong et al. (2023, IEEE TAC, arXiv:2209.07104) derive noise-covariance identification conditions using measurement differences, stationarity, and known system matrices.
Blevins (2017, Econometric Theory) formulates matrix-log aliasing and rank-checkable restrictions for equispaced continuous-time models.
Ding–Qiu–Chen (2009, Automatica) show that multiple nonuniformly sampled discrete models can uniquely reconstruct a continuous-time system.
Mu et al. (2015, Automatica) connect irregular sampling to SISO identifiability, convergent algorithms, and sampling-dependent excitation.
Hauenstein–Sottile (2012), Chernozhukov–Hong–Tamer (2007), Drton (2009), and Andrews–Cheng (2012) provide adjacent tools for certified finite roots, set inference, singular limits, and weak identification.
The unoccupied combinations above are bounded-search inferences: no inspected paper proves the shared-E unpaired-snapshot stabilizer theorem, its certified finite-branch inference, or its nonuniform/joint-noise variants.
